inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ~1,290m (Q2 2026 10-Q weighted diluted 1,287m, rounded up for unvested awards). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. No non-SBC issuance modelled.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement: SBC add-back $535m + taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards $158m (financing) = $693m; no combined company figure published. H1-2026 run-rate is higher ($442m SBC + $154m award taxes), hence the 0.20% forward path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.8 gives a cost of equity of ~8.3%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (BBB), after-tax ~4.3%. Market-value weights are ~65% equity ($115bn) and ~35% debt ($61bn), giving ~6.9%, rounded up to 7.25% for the leverage (3.7x net debt/EBITDA). Regulatory risk is charged in the scenario paths and weights, not in the rate. One WACC for all scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: store rent is inside operating expense, so EBITDA is already post-rent. Operating lease liabilities (~$17bn) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is borrowings only. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are immaterial (<0.1% of net income); ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, consolidated. Routing: CVS straddles the 'operating company' and 'insurer' rows. About 70% of revenue and most of the earnings power comes from Caremark PBM, Oak Street/Signify and retail pharmacy, which are cash-flow operating businesses. Aetna (Health Care Benefits, ~30% of revenue) is a managed-care insurer whose earnings are underwriting margin on premiums, not book compounding. Like UNH/CI/ELV, integrated managed care is valued on consolidated cash flow, not BVPS x P/B; a sum-of-parts was not attempted because no segment-level cash flows were extracted (no text filings in Extracted/, XBRL only). Insurance treatment: (1) Aetna's net investment income stays inside EBITDA as operating income, because the portfolio backs claim reserves and statutory capital. (2) Consistent with (1), the ~$20bn+ of long-term investments is NOT added to the bridge (matching-asset rule). (3) Balance-sheet cash is netted in full against debt, although part of the $11.3bn sits in regulated insurance subsidiaries. This offsets (2) and is flagged as a risk: counting only parent cash would lower value by ~$5-7/share. Interest income is not stripped: the company has net debt, not net cash. FY2025 GAAP EBITDA ($9.3bn, 2.3% margin) is depressed by the Q3-2025 Health Care Delivery (Oak Street) goodwill impairment and MA reserve charges, so it is not a base. Year 1 (FY2026) is built from guidance instead: GAAP EPS $6.84-7.04 x ~1.285bn diluted shares = ~$8.9bn NI; /0.75 = ~$11.9bn pretax; plus ~$3.0bn interest = ~$14.9bn EBIT; plus ~$4.5bn D&A = ~$19.4bn EBITDA on ~$426bn revenue = ~4.55%. Cross-checks: H1-2026 EBITDA was $11.6bn, and H2 is seasonally weaker for MA. OCF guidance of at least $11.5bn less ~$2.9bn capex is ~$8.6bn levered FCF, against ~$12bn unlevered from the component build less ~$2.3bn after-tax interest. The ~$1bn gap is restructuring, opioid-settlement and reserve timing cash. Buybacks: zero in FY2025 and H1-2026 (suspended to delever; $3.0bn in FY2024), so the flat share count is currently a modelling convention the company is not funding. Horizon 10 years because margins are still recovering toward the 2028 target through year 3-4.

equity_bridge.note: 2022 national settlement of ~$5bn payable over ~10 years from 2023. Remaining balance is estimated at ~$3.5bn at mid-2026, not read from a filing: no text filings are extracted for CVS. Charged in 2022 GAAP, so it is absent from the forward EBITDA and deducted here once.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: revenue CAGR (7.6-8.4%) tempered for low-margin GLP-1/specialty pass-through inflation and pharmacy store rationalization; equity and EPS CAGRs rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~1.6%) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (~8%) and EPS CAGR (~-24%). Equity is flat because of dividends plus FY2022-24 buybacks, and because FY2022/FY2025 impairments and opioid charges hit retained earnings. EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs run from pre-crisis to the FY2025 MA-margin and impairment trough. None of the three is a forward growth proxy.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF − SBC − equity-award taxes (no interest-income strip: net debt). FY2020 $12,940m, FY2022 $12,633m, FY2025 $7,114m. The owner-FCF CAGR is only ~0.8-1pp below reported, so SBC is not what drove the FCF decline: that was the Aetna MA cost-trend shock of 2023-25. H1-2026 reported FCF was $9,054m, already above FY2025's full year.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands at the midpoint of raised guidance. Aetna reaches roughly its target margin by 2028-29, but the consolidated EBITDA margin plateaus at 5.0%, below the FY2019-21 6-7%, because revenue mix keeps shifting to low-margin specialty/GLP-1 pass-through dispensing and PBM rebate economics are partly given back under the FTC settlement and state pass-through laws.
base.da_pct_note: D&A includes ~$1.6bn/yr of acquired-intangible amortization (Aetna, Oak Street, Signify), which rolls down over time. D&A converges toward capex.
base.cash_tax_note: 26% cash rate, above the ~21% federal statutory rate. It covers state taxes and non-deductible acquired-intangible amortization (Aetna was a stock deal). FY2023 cash taxes ran ~32% of pretax.
base.wc_note: Positive capture: claim reserves and pharmacy payables grow with premiums and scripts. FY2019-23 OCF consistently exceeded NI + D&A.
base.cap_note: 13x cap binds (Gordon ~21.6x at 7.25%/2.5%). Structurally slow, politically regulated conglomerate; today's EV/unlevered-FCF is ~14x.

bull.narrative: Management delivers the mid-teens Adjusted EPS CAGR to 2028. MBR normalizes, star ratings recover and 2027 quality bonuses land. Oak Street reaches breakeven and then contributes. Caremark retains its book through the FTC settlement with limited rebate give-back, and Rite Aid/Walgreens script transfers lift pharmacy volume. The consolidated margin recovers to 5.6%, still below the pre-2022 peak.

bear.narrative: The MA recovery stalls in H2-2026/2027 as utilization stays elevated and CMS risk-adjustment and rate changes bite. State pass-through/anti-spread laws and follow-on federal PBM reform take a durable slice of Caremark's rebate and spread economics. Retail keeps shrinking under reimbursement pressure, and Oak Street stays a drag. The consolidated margin drifts to 3.9%, near the FY2024 trough level ex-impairment, and a lower 11x cap reflects the break-up and regulatory overhang.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-midpoint FY2026, then an Aetna margin recovery that plateaus at a 5.0% consolidated EBITDA margin: below the FY2019-21 peak because of pass-through-heavy pharmacy mix and partial PBM rebate give-back. Revenue growth decelerates from 6% to 3%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Mid-teens Adjusted EPS CAGR to 2028 delivered: MBR normalizes, star ratings and quality bonuses recover, Oak Street turns profitable, and Caremark comes through the FTC settlement intact. The margin rebuilds to 5.6%.
scenario_narratives.bear: MA cost trend and CMS policy reverse the 2026 recovery, state and federal PBM reform compresses Caremark, and retail keeps shrinking. The margin slides to 3.9% with growth of 2-3%, on a lower exit multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear is raised from the 15% default to 30% because the thesis rests on regulator-controlled variables: CMS MA rates and risk adjustment, and state and federal PBM reform that could force structural separation. The MA recovery has only two quarters of evidence. Base is held at 50% since FY2026 guidance has been raised twice with an OCF raise behind it. Bull is cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right: MBR, Oak Street breakeven, PBM retention and no further regulatory give-back.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Consolidated owner-FCF DCF on an integrated managed-care/PBM/pharmacy conglomerate, with year 1 anchored to raised FY2026 guidance rather than the impairment-depressed FY2025 trough. SBC is small (~0.2% of revenue), so the house and street bases sit close together. The value case is margin normalization to a level still well below pre-2022, against leverage and regulator-controlled risks. The multiples sanity check trips against FY2025 trough actuals; on FY2026-guidance and mid-cycle denominators the implied P/E (~19.5x) and EV/EBITDA (~11.4x) sit inside the 10-year range (see sanity_check_note).
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path is the whole valuation: each 0.1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly $5-6/share on ~$550bn terminal revenue.
Part of the $11.3bn cash sits in regulated insurance subsidiaries. Netting only parent cash would lower IV by ~$5-7/share (partly offset by the excluded investment portfolio).
Opioid settlement remainder ($3.5bn) is an estimate, not read from a filing.
PBM reform (pass-through, delinking, forced divestiture) could move Caremark economics outside the bear path.
Leverage (~3.7x net debt/EBITDA): a renewed MA shock with a ratings downgrade would pressure refinancing and the dividend.
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note: The 2026-09-26 multiples sanity check tripped on an implied P/E of 139x against a 24x 10-year average, with implied EV/EBITDA of 26x against 11.95x. Both are artefacts of the denominator. The check divides the weighted IV by FY2025 actuals: SBC-adjusted EPS of ~$0.88 and EBITDA of $9.3bn. Those figures are the trough year, depressed by the Q3-2025 Oak Street goodwill impairment and the MA reserve charges. The valuation is not built on them. Year 1 is the FY2026 guidance midpoint (~4.55% EBITDA margin, ~$19.4bn), and the terminal is capped at 13x unlevered FCF (bear 11x), which implies ~8.1x terminal EBITDA, below the 10-year average of 11.95x. On a normalized denominator the weighted IV implies 19.5x FY2026 GAAP-guidance EPS less SBC (16.7x adjusted), 26.4x FY2019-24 mid-cycle SBC-adjusted EPS, and 11.4x FY2026 EBITDA less SBC. All three are inside the historical range. Fix applied: priority 1, a mid-cycle/normalized basis, was already in place and was verified. The exit-multiple cap (priority 4) already binds below the historical-average EV/EBITDA. No driver path was changed, because moving margins or the WACC to pass a test measured against a trough denominator would be a fabricated fix. The trip is expected to persist until FY2026 actuals replace FY2025 in the check.
